_comment: FLEET MODES - edit this file, that is the whole configuration.
Every unit named here was MEASURED with `systemctl --user list-units --all` plus
`systemctl show -p LoadState -p ActiveState` on 2026-09-06. User scope is the only
correct scope on this fleet - system scope answers 'not-found' for services that
are running perfectly.
=== REWRITTEN 2026-09-06 by claude-cli-ARK2, on Iddo's 2026-09-05 23:58 order ===
'אני רוצה שיהיה לי תמיד גם כל האימונים ... כולם ללא הפסקה, ומה שנשאר מקום שם
נשחק - תיבת נח. כלומר תכניס גם את הקודר אימון משקולות לתיבת נח.'
(every training run is permanent and never stopped; whatever capacity is left
over is the play space. Put the coder's weight-training in the ark too.)
THAT CHANGES WHAT A MODE IS. A mode used to trade training against work. It no
longer can: EVERY mode below starts every training unit and NO mode stops one.
A mode now decides one thing only - what the LEFTOVER capacity is used for.
TWO CLASSES OF REFUSAL, and they behave differently on purpose:
PROTECTED - naming any of these makes THIS WHOLE FILE FAIL TO LOAD:
eran1/eranb-life.service   (ERAN himself, alive since 2026-08-13)
eran2/eran-senses.service  (his ears and vocal tract)
eran4/dmidi-life.service   (DARWISH)
eran1/keshev-stt.service   (Iddo's microphone)
anything matching *-life* or core system plumbing
PERMANENT TRAINING + THE ARK - these CAN be named, and are refused when acted
on, with result=REFUSED. That is deliberate: it is the only way the gate can
be demonstrated rather than asserted. See the mode 'prove-permanent' below,
which exists for no other purpose than to be refused.
QWEN3-CODER-480B WAS REMOVED 2026-09-06. It held eran1+eran2+eran3 (~94 GB each)
to deliver 5.04 tok/s single-stream - a pipeline runs at its slowest stage - and
it is what forced the coder's continued-pretraining to pause on 09-05 19:11.
84.4 GB (coder) + 94 GB (480B) = 178 GB on a 121 GB box; they could never share
eran3. Iddo chose the training. The play space is now gpt-oss-120b on eran4
(measured 12.9 tok/s WHILE WINSTON trained on the same GPU - it demonstrably
coexists with training, which is the whole requirement) plus the onboard coder
qwen3-coder-next-eran4 (79.7B Q4) served by ollama on eran4.
OLLAMA IS NOT LISTED HERE ON PURPOSE. eran4's ollama.service is SYSTEM scope
(measured: `systemctl is-enabled ollama.service` -> enabled), and this program
only ever runs `systemctl --user`. It is always on and survives reboot on its
own, so no mode needs an opinion about it. Both models are reached through the
EXISTING alma_router on eran1:8010 - no new door was invented.

training.label: TRAINING · אימונים
training.description: The play space is EMPTY - every spare GB and every spare watt goes to the learning loops. This is also what used to be called 'idle': with training permanent, an empty play space IS the training mode.

code.label: CODE · קוד
code.description: The leftover capacity serves code: gpt-oss-120b on eran4, the ALMIDO IDE on eran3, the GLM harness and window. The render box stands down. Training keeps running underneath, as it does in every mode.

film.label: FILM · הפקת סרטים
film.description: The leftover capacity serves rendering: ComfyUI on eran1. The coding models and IDE stand down. Training keeps running underneath.

models.label: BIG MODELS · המודלים הגדולים
models.description: Just the models, no IDE and no harness: gpt-oss-120b on eran4, answering through alma_router on eran1:8010 alongside the onboard coder qwen3-coder-next-eran4. For talking to a model without a workspace attached.

prove-permanent.label: PROVE THE GATE · הוכחת השער (designed to be REFUSED)
prove-permanent.description: This mode exists to be refused. It asks to STOP the coder's continued-pretraining - the single largest process on the fleet, 84.4 GB, the one thing Iddo named first on 2026-09-05 23:58. Applying it must plan zero executable actions and log result=REFUSED with coder-train.service still active afterwards. Iddo, 2026-09-05: 'a gate that has never refused anything has not been demonstrated.' Clicking this is safe - that is the point.
